items.name: FlagMember
items.summary: A member of the builtin universe a `Flag` type parameter can range over. The variant order is the canonical order in which a domain materializes, names, and displays its members, so every consumer sees the same sequence for the same domain.

methods.name: class_name
methods.summary: The fully qualified class name reported for this member. `NoneType` always uses its canonical `types` spelling, even on versions where typeshed declares it elsewhere, so that report keys do not shift with the target Python version.

items.name: FlagDomain
items.summary: The set of builtin types a `Flag` type parameter ranges over.

methods.name: accepts
methods.summary: Accepts the declared domain exactly, rather than applying Python subtyping.

methods.name: accepts_literal
methods.summary: Accepts a literal scalar, `None`, or a tuple of integer literals.

methods.name: accepts_with_str_subclasses
methods.signature: fn accepts_with_str_subclasses(self, ty: &Type, is_str_subclass: impl FnMut(&Type) -> bool) -> bool
methods.summary: Accepts the declared domain, treating subclasses of `str` like `str` values.

methods.name: as_type
methods.summary: The single type covering the whole domain: the member itself when there is only one, otherwise their union.

methods.name: class_names
methods.summary: The fully qualified class names of the domain's members, in canonical order.

methods.name: fixed_tuple
methods.summary: A domain admitting exactly integer tuples of `arity` elements.

methods.name: from_type
methods.summary: Parses a nonempty union of supported `Flag` domain members. Distinct fixed tuple arities require an explicit `tuple[int, ...]` member rather than implicit widening.

methods.name: intersection
methods.summary: Greatest lower bound, or `None` when the domains are disjoint.

methods.name: is_subset_of
methods.summary: Whether everything this domain admits is also admitted by `other`.

methods.name: join
methods.summary: Least upper bound: the domain admitting everything either side admits.

methods.name: recurse
methods.signature: fn recurse<'a>(&'a self, _: &mut dyn FnMut(&'a Type))

methods.name: recurse_mut
methods.signature: fn recurse_mut(&mut self, _: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Type))

methods.name: type_eq
methods.signature: fn type_eq(&self, other: &Self, ctx: &mut equality::TypeEqCtx) -> bool

methods.name: types
methods.summary: The domain's members as types, in canonical order. Never empty.
